restaurants.name: Fishnets
restaurants.summary: Omakase-level technique without the hushed ceremony: sushi, shareable tuna katsu and Japanese-influenced plates using Australian produce.
restaurants.cons: Set menus start around $92pp; the narrow neighbourhood room fills quickly.
comments: Fish quality feels special-occasion level.
Tuna katsu is the share plate people remember.
Service is polished without being stiff.
Wine pairings suit the seafood-heavy menu.
The unusual mapo gelato divides opinion—in a fun way.

restaurants.name: The Hideaway
restaurants.summary: A moody underground restaurant and cocktail bar inspired by New York’s late-night dining scene, with live music as dinner rolls into drinks.
restaurants.cons: Premium pricing and dim lighting; the hidden downstairs entrance is easy to miss.
comments: The basement setting feels genuinely transportive.
Tableside beef tartare is a recurring highlight.
Cocktails and live music make it a full night out.
Staff are attentive even as the room gets louder.
Several diners note the bill climbs quickly.

restaurants.name: Trattoria Da Orazio
restaurants.summary: Orazio D’Elia returns to his former Rushcutters Bay kitchen with an all-regions Italian trattoria built for lively, generous group meals.
restaurants.cons: Fresh opening means limited review history; busy launch-period bookings are likely.
comments: The menu goes beyond the usual red-sauce classics.
Share-style portions work well for groups.
The room has an energetic neighbourhood feel.
Pizza and handmade pasta lead early favourites.
Prime dinner times are already hard to secure.

restaurants.name: Stanley at Manly Wharf
restaurants.summary: Louis Tikaram’s 212-seat Hong Kong-inspired waterfront restaurant promises live seafood, Cantonese dishes and tableside Peking duck.
restaurants.cons: Not open at snapshot date; hype is based on previews, so service and value are untested.
comments: The Manly Wharf location is the headline attraction.
Tableside duck service should suit celebrations.
A custom duck oven signals serious intent.
The 212-seat scale could make it lively rather than intimate.
No diner consensus exists until doors officially open.

restaurants.name: Da Orazio Pasticceria
restaurants.summary: A Roman-style bakery and all-day stop from the Da Orazio team—known for maritozzi, focaccia sandwiches and polished Italian pastries.
restaurants.cons: Industrial-area location is less convenient without a car; Tripadvisor’s sample is very small.
comments: Cream-filled maritozzi are the social-media magnet.
Focaccia texture earns repeat praise.
Coffee holds its own beside the pastries.
Popular items can sell out later in the day.
The industrial setting is a practical drawback.

restaurants.name: Bar Bruno
restaurants.summary: A compact Italian wine bar where snacks, handmade pasta and a sharp by-the-glass list matter more than white-tablecloth ceremony.
restaurants.cons: Small room, close tables and limited space for larger groups; peak sessions feel busy.
comments: Pasta is the dish category most likely to impress.
The by-the-glass wine list rewards curiosity.
Staff recommendations make ordering easy.
The close-set room feels cosy to some, cramped to others.
Best suited to pairs or small groups.
